thread.title: Qualcomm Earnings May Not Be Strong Enough to Lift the Stock

author: Barron's
title: Qualcomm Earnings May Not Be Strong Enough to Lift the Stock
text:
Photograph by Brent Lewin/Bloomberg There isn't much more Qualcomm can do to increase the company's profits, according to Bank of America Merrill Lynch.
The firm's analyst Tal Liani lowered his rating on Qualcomm ( QCOM ) stock to Neutral from Buy, predicting the technology company will report profits below expectations next year.
"Our model suggests that management has exhausted most opportunities for P&L restructuring, yet earnings upside is not likely to be sufficient to increase the share price," Liani wrote on Wednesday. "In addition, smartphone demand is softening and we reduce our estimates accordingly."
The analyst lowered his price target for Qualcomm stock to $70 from $75. Liani slightly raised his fiscal 2018 and 2019 earnings-per-share estimates to $3.63 and $4.21, respectively, from $3.60 and $4.18, but cut the 2020 EPS estimate to $4.97 from $5.64. The fiscal 2019 EPS estimate of $4.21 is materially lower than the $4.45 FactSet consensus.
Qualcomm's stock is down 0.7%, to $62.73 on Wednesday. Its shares have declined about 2% year to date.
The analyst also cited the uncertainty surrounding licensing disagreements with two key customers - Huawei and Apple ( AAPL ). He had no forecast on when those disputes will be resolved.
Liani also said the arrival of fifth-generation wireless technology will take time to benefit the smartphone-chip maker.
"5G is not expected to be a major driver in the foreseeable future, with meaningful device shipments only starting in 12-18 months," he wrote.
Qualcomm is slated to report its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings on Nov. 7 after the close.
